name: Platformer
summary: A course of levels over the world's own streets, ending at its people's homes and workplaces: start, goal, checkpoints and par, every step a traversal movement, a fall back to the furthest checkpoint, and up to three stars a level.

parameters.doc: levels a generated course has when the world's platformer section names no count (5); an authored count, or authored levels, win

extensionPoints.signature: WorldIR.platformer {levels: [{id, start, goal, goalKind?, subject?, checkpoints?, par?}], levelCount?, runnerModes?}
extensionPoints.doc: authored levels over the world's link graph; with none a course is generated (src/platformer/course.ts)
whether this jump can be made from here: the engine's geometry answers, core decides
the run, the jump arc and the landing are the engine's
read with readPlatformerBlock (src/platformer/platformer-save.ts), restored with PlatformerDirector.restore over the same world's course

assistant.summary: src/platformer/course.ts builds the course (courseForWorld: authored levels, else generated over the streets, homes and workplaces); PlatformerDirector (src/game-engine/logic/PlatformerDirector.ts) moves runners only through TraversalPlanner and remembers the level, checkpoints, run cost and best clears; src/platformer/platformer-save.ts is the extensions.platformer block. The engine draws the level select, the timer and the stars, and answers the probe.
notes: Every step is one traversal movement to an adjacent place: step(runner, to). A fall is respawn(runner): the KB puts the runner at the furthest checkpoint this run touched, or the start.
Stars are integers from the run's cost against par: within par 3, within half as much again 2, else 1.
Runner modes (walk, jump) come from the world's platformer section; without jump no doorstep is reached and the generated course is empty.
The side-view rig (GAP-RCP2) and the recipe-plan build of the level's pieces (P9j.core-build-plan) are separate rows: do not place pieces from this pack.
doNot: Move a runner outside the director: a teleport skips the checkpoints and the cost the stars read.
Store a level's stars for a run under way: they are derived when the level is cleared.
